transcript: Meeting header: 2025-08-13 10:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Lena Ortiz, Marcus Chen (Redwood) — Aisha Khan, Tom Reyes, Priya Singh (Vertex Health)

Summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results (latency and throughput) vs Vertex's current baseline provider. Discussed results, variability, config tuning (batching, quantization), and next steps to run tail tests and schedule deeper technical session.
Topics: 1) Results overview 2) Tail latency concerns 3) Config changes attempted 4) Tests to run next
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everybody, welcome back — quick check, is this a good time for the 45?
[00:06] Aisha Khan: yep, good to go, we have about 45, thanks lena
[00:12] Marcus Chen: i'll jump straight into the benchmark slide, we ran the same model family you asked — redwood-opt-7b quantized q4_0 vs their baseline 7b float on BaselineCloud
[00:22] Priya Singh: quick clarif, the baseline's VMs were the ones you used earlier, right, the ones with 8 v100-equivalent?

[00:28] Marcus Chen: yes that's correct, baseline used their shared v100 pool; our Dedicated tests ran on A100v4 reserved nodes, configured with continuous batching off for latency runs and on for throughput runs
[00:36] Tom Reyes: one note, our staging traffic is mix of short and long sequences, 40% under 128 tokens, 40% 128-512, 20% above 512 — that was the distribution we sent

[00:44] Marcus Chen: perfect, we used that distribution for the mixed-run. Results high-level: p50 latency for short seqs — Redwood: ~42ms, BaselineCloud: ~58ms. For medium (256) p95 Redwood: ~210ms vs Baseline: ~280ms. For long (512) p95 Redwood: ~480ms vs Baseline: ~730ms
[01:05] Aisha Khan: those p95 numbers look promising but the p99 for long tails?

[01:10] Marcus Chen: p99 for 512 tokens we've seen around 820ms on Redwood in our Dedicated config, Baseline p99 was ~1.3s in their shared infra. There's variability depending on concurrent requests and batching windows
[01:24] Lena Ortiz: to be clear — these were our stock quantization settings (q4_0) and default kernel selection; we can push q4_k and see small latency wins, but need to re-run quality checks
[01:34] Tom Reyes: what's the throughput delta? For peak we care about tokens/sec more than single-request latency sometimes

[01:39] Marcus Chen: throughput (mixed seqs, continuous batching enabled): Redwood Dedicated sustained ~18k tokens/sec per node, Baseline sustained ~11k tokens/sec. For request-per-second (short seq focus) Redwood hit ~620 req/s vs Baseline ~380 req/s
[01:52] Priya Singh: cost implications? if we switch to Dedicated reserve is that a hard increase?

[01:56] Lena Ortiz: depends on commit. In our preliminary pricing the per-token unit cost drops about 20% at the reserved tier compared to the hosted baseline. But we'll share a detailed spreadsheet — Marcus will include burst config costs
[02:08] Aisha Khan: one concern is tail latency spikes during garbage collection or kernel swaps — did you see any periodic spikes?

[02:14] Marcus Chen: yes small spikes early in the run when kernels compile, that's why we do warm-up. There were also occasional KV-cache misses when we changed the prompt prefix distribution which increased p99 by ~150ms intermittently
[02:26] Tom Reyes: we saw that on BaselineCloud too, but their p99 spikes were more frequent at scale, likely their noisy neighbor problem
[02:32] Marcus Chen: exactly. Also the routing: our smart routing avoided overloaded hosts; baseline had less sophisticated fallback so you get more variance

[02:39] Lena Ortiz: i want to call out the tuning we applied this week — Marcus turned on prefix caching for the 60% of requests with repeated context, and we adjusted batching window to 8ms for latency-sensitive lanes
[02:48] Marcus Chen: right, that gave ~12% p95 improvement on medium sequences but slightly reduced throughput for heavy-batch runs. tradeoff is latency vs max tokens/sec
[02:58] Aisha Khan: any quality regressions from q4_0 quant?

[03:01] Marcus Chen: for the prompts you provided the automated eval shows minimal diffs in top-1 for 95% cases; we'll share the eval artifacts. edge cases exist for some math or rare tokens but not in your core use cases
[03:12] Priya Singh: good. for the next runs can we get a factory reset scenario — i.e., cold kernels and cold cache to see worst-case startup tail?
[03:19] Marcus Chen: yes we can schedule a cold-start run. that'll show the compile overhead (~150-250ms early per host) and the first-request kv misses. We'll annotate results
[03:25] Tom Reyes: on the infra side — network egress between our VPC and Redwood's Dedicated nodes, did you measure cross-region variances? We have users in eu-west and us-east
[03:33] Marcus Chen: these tests run in us-east only; cross-region adds ~30-70ms depending on region. We can run eu-west dedicated nodes if you want similar numbers
[03:41] Aisha Khan: yes please, we want parity across regions. Also we need SOC2 docs and audit logs for compliance — is that still in your enterprise kit?
[03:48] Lena Ortiz: absolutely, i'll attach SOC2 and KMS/HSM integration docs after this call. we'll also include RBAC and SSO guides
[03:55] Priya Singh: Circling back — the baseline provider claims autoscale plus cheaper spot pricing. How much of our wins are hardware vs software?

[04:01] Marcus Chen: good question — part is hardware (A100v4 > older V100), but a big part is our runtime optimizations: attention kernels, KV cache efficiency, and smart batching. In side-by-side with identical GPU class we still see ~15% latency improvement because of kernel selection and lower scheduling jitter
[04:16] Aisha Khan: can you explain the kernel selection bit — sometimes our infra team calls it kuvernates scheduling? (laughs)

[04:21] Marcus Chen: haha, kubernetes — kernel selection is internal: we pick optimized routines per sequence length and model op pattern. it's why quant + correct kernels matter; wrong kernel can add 30-80ms
[04:31] Tom Reyes: any known incompatibilities with our on-prem options if we go private later?
[04:35] Lena Ortiz: Private supports similar runtime but you'd manage the infra; some kernel paths need specific drivers. we'll provide a checklist for on-prem requirements
[04:42] Aisha Khan: what about degradation modes — if Dedicated saturates do you fallback to hosted or baseline variants?
[04:48] Marcus Chen: yes smart routing allows fallback to smaller model variants or Hosted API depending on policy. we can configure cost-first or latency-first fallback policies
[04:56] Priya Singh: ok next i'd like to see a side-by-side CSV of p50/p95/p99 across seq buckets (<=128, 129-512, >512) with concurrency levels 50, 200, 500

[05:04] Marcus Chen: that's in progress — i'll run the 50/200/500 concurrency matrices and attach the CSVs. the 500 concurrency runs will show the tightest difference in throughput — expect Redwood to scale more linearly
[05:14] Aisha Khan: any quick wins we should toggle now? e.g., reduce batch window or enforce prefix caching aggressively

[05:19] Marcus Chen: immediate wins: reduce batching window to 5ms for latency lanes, enforce prefix caching for repeated contexts, and enable q4_k for a re-run with eval. we'll need 24–48h to run full matrices
[05:29] Tom Reyes: fine with me — we can carve a maintenance window in staging tomorrow night for the tests
[05:35] Lena Ortiz: great. i'll recap next steps at the end. any other questions?
[05:38] Priya Singh: just one on SLAs — if we hit committed latency SLOs, what's the penalty?
[05:43] Lena Ortiz: for Dedicated reserved contracts we include uptime SLA and latency targets in the contract; penalties are negotiated per deal — i'll send template language
[05:49] Aisha Khan: ok good. also please include the security addendum for data residency
[05:53] Lena Ortiz: noted, will include

[06:00] Marcus Chen: one more technical point — we noticed a small tail correlation with GC cycles in their baseline provider when memory pressure hits. on Redwood our KV cache eviction is more deterministic, so tails are less correlated
[06:12] Tom Reyes: that's useful to know; reduces jitter for our user-facing latency SLOs
[06:16] Marcus Chen: i'll include per-run GC telemetry in the CSVs so you can see correlation
[06:20] Aisha Khan: perfect. PR for demo — could we get a short recorded run that shows both the cold-start and warmed runs side-by-side? helps our execs
[06:28] Lena Ortiz: yes we can capture a screen + perf graphs, we'll upload to the shared folder
[06:32] Priya Singh: timeline — when can we expect all artifacts?
[06:35] Marcus Chen: cold + warm matrices and csvs by 2025-08-20, SOC2 and security docs by 2025-08-15, pricing by 2025-08-15

[06:41] Lena Ortiz: ok final recap of next steps — Marcus runs the 1k tail tests, does 50/200/500 concurrency matrices, and shares CSV + GC telemetry by 8/20. Lena sends pricing and security docs by 8/15. Vertex shares sample traffic and opens staging access by 8/18. Schedule deep dive week of 8/25.
[06:55] Aisha Khan: sounds good, thanks everyone
[06:58] Tom Reyes: thx, bye
[07:01] Lena Ortiz: thanks all, will follow up in email — bye
